items.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: Dad was a bass player and a part time musician who always worked doing casual jobs

ctx.x: And what led you into this thing? Was it just by virtue of the fact that you played the cornet or the trumpet that you — or did you come from a musical —

I came from a musical family. Dad was a bass player and a part time musician who always worked doing casual jobs, what we used to call club dates, weddings, that sort of thing. He had a large record collection, and played records. One of my fondest memories as a kid is being able to wake up and lay in bed and listen to music for an hour. You know, it just was there. It was always around me. And Dad had a magnificent collection of 78s which he didn’t mind, you know, an eight or a nine year old going through and…
Was one of your first big moments — this is something I read and I don’t know if it’s true — you did a concert with the New York Jazz Repertory and you were doing some Bix tunes or something?
